chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: Ivory Joe Hunter's equipped bus and Nat Towles charging rent
summary: Ivory Joe Hunter bought a specially equipped bus from his royalties, and Nat Towles charged his players $35 a month to sleep on his bus.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: But, of course, we didn't have the title. That's it. This brings up a good question, a good statement, rather. I was just reading about a guy that passed here recently. You remember the guy that wrote a lot of tunes called Ivory Joe Hunter?

Well, he was a smart guy, man. He bought a bus for his band. Well, he got so many royalties, so much money from the tunes that he had written, of course, he had a lot of hits, and, man, he bought a bus that was quite expensive, and I had the pleasure of going through that bus, and he showed it to me one time. And he had his little office in the bus, had it made up special, and this particular bus that he had, they had their own beds and everything in it. It was really specially equipped. Not like the Newark Charter Company.
Well, that's what I was wondering, if --

It was Specially equipped -- the Newark Charter Company -- and it had 32 seats in it. It was just one of those straight up type seats. They go back, you know, you can lean back, but you're still in a seat. But Ivory Joe had this thing equipped, man, so the boys didn't have the -- when they stayed overnight somewhere, they stayed in the bus, you know.
Yeah. I know a couple of the bands I played on in the '50's, we had buses that way, that were specially built. You had record players and the whole thing.
Yeah, they were really equipped, so that it was an interesting thing, and they had, naturally, air conditioning. They had places to cook and those things.
I know there's another bandleader out of Omaha, Nebraska, Nat Towles. He always had his own bus. And, man, he used to charge the guys so much a month to stay in the buses.

Because they had their own beds and everything like that, and if I remember correctly, I had some musicians that joined my band out of his band, and they used to tell us about it, man, that Nat would charge the guys $35.00 a month, you know, like an apartment.
Yeah, even when he came off the road, he would park the bus, you know, in an area in Omaha where, you know, you could park, and the guys would still stay there. So actually that was quite a deal.
